description: A sixteen-step trigger sequencer with thirty-two stored programs, clocked or addressed by voltage

params.text: Turns that step on or off
Sets how many steps the sequence runs through, 1 to 16
Chooses whether the jack below it advances the sequence on each trigger or addresses a step directly by voltage
Sets which step a reset jumps to, 1 to 16; in TURING mode it attenuates the output voltage instead
Selects one of the thirty-two programs, 0 to 31; the choice only takes effect when SET is pressed, unless AUTO is on
Reloads the selected program, discarding any edits made since it was stored
Double-click to store the current sequence and its settings into the selected program
Applies the pending program change, and applies any step edits made to a pending program
Applies a program change the moment it is made, instead of waiting for the SET button

inputs.text: Advances the sequence on each trigger, or addresses a step with 0-10V spread across the set length, depending on the switch above it
Held above 1V, each clock steps backwards instead of forwards; it is read in clock mode only
Runs the sequencer for as long as it is held high, or toggles it on a trigger with Run Input set to Trig
A trigger here jumps to the step the RST knob sets; it is read in clock mode only
Lengthens the sequence, 0-10V covering all sixteen steps, added to the STEPS knob
Selects the program by voltage, or steps to the next stored one on each trigger with Prog Input type set to Trig

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse on the steps that are on, or a held gate or a clock-width pulse under Output type; in TURING mode it carries a voltage worked out from the on steps instead

notes: a program is only saved by double-clicking STOR; editing the steps and moving on loses the changes.
in TURING mode the sequence is read as a register of bits and turned into a voltage, the way randLoops does it, so the output stops being a trigger.
menu: Randomize Steps — turns all sixteen steps on or off at random
Output type: Trig, Gate, Clock Width — chooses whether an on step sends a 1ms pulse, a gate lasting the whole step, or a pulse the length of the incoming clock's high part
Reverse Input Voltage: Positive, Negative — chooses whether REV runs the sequence backwards above 1V or below -1V
Run Input: Gate, Trig — chooses whether the RUN jack runs the sequencer while held high or toggles it on each trigger
Reset on Run — resets the step when the sequencer goes from stopped to running
Don't advance — makes the first clock after a reset hold on the reset step rather than moving off it
Prog Input type: CV, Trig — chooses whether the PROG jack reads a voltage or steps to the next stored program on each trigger
Scan Last Prog — reads every program again and reports the highest one that holds anything
Copy Sequence — puts the current sequence on a clipboard shared with other trigSeq and randLoops modules
Paste Sequence — takes a sequence off that clipboard; it is shown as a plain label when the clipboard is empty
TURING MODE — reads the sixteen steps as register bits and puts out a voltage built from them, which turns on the Bit Resolution and Voltage progression items
Bit Resolution: 8 bit, 16 bit — sets how many of the steps the TURING voltage is built from
Voltage progression: 2x (std.), 1.3x, Fibonacci — sets how much each further bit is worth in the TURING voltage
DISK operations — a submenu with Load trigSeq PRESET and Save trigSeq PRESET, which read and write all thirty-two programs and the module's settings as one file
Initialize on Start — returns to the first step when Rack loads a patch, instead of resuming where the sequence stopped
